description: Flattens a RawBundle into the base (pre-derived-score) feature frame: identity, price, review counts, owners band, size, achievement/language/platform/DLC counts, early-access fields, deck compatibility, genres, categories. Records which fields were absent per row.
docstring:
Build the base feature frame from raw payloads.

Args:
    bundle: Output of parse_raw_bundle.

Returns:
    A DataFrame indexed by appid with columns: name, developer, publisher, release_date (raw string, unparsed), release_date_parsed (date or NaT), price_usd, is_free, review_count, review_positive_pct, owners_estimate_low/mid/high, size_bytes, achievement_count, language_count, platform_count, dlc_count, is_early_access, early_access_days, deck_compat, genres_json, categories_json, app_type, missing_fields_json (a per-row JSON list of feature names that were absent from the source payload and therefore not yet imputed -- imputation itself happens later, in compute_complexity_score / impute_missing_at_median, not here).

Source precedence for review_count (per the module's own invariant): the Steam reviews endpoint value is used when appdetails/reviews succeeded; SteamSpy's review-derived figure (positive+negative) is used only as a fallback when the reviews fetch failed or is absent for that appid. The column review_count_source ('steam_reviews' | 'steamspy_fallback') records which was used.

Rows whose app_type (from appdetails.data.type) is not 'game' are still included in the returned frame but flagged via a boolean is_game column set to False; dropping them is build_enriched_frame's responsibility (so the dropped-row tally can be counted at the composition level), not normalize_features'.
preconditions: bundle.steamspy is non-empty for at least the appids also present in appdetails (should always hold by RawBundle's own postcondition)
postconditions: One row per appid present in bundle.steamspy (the full candidate-adjacent universe, not just successfully detailed apps), so density/competition-relevant counts are not silently lost for an appid whose detail fetch failed
review_positive_pct is in [0, 1] or NaN, never a raw percentage-as-integer (e.g. 87 instead of 0.87)
size_bytes, achievement_count, language_count, platform_count, dlc_count are non-negative integers or NaN, never negative

edge_cases.input: appdetails payload has success=false for an appid
edge_cases.expected_behavior: is_game=False, most derived columns NaN/None, appid retained in the frame with whatever SteamSpy bulk fields are available

edge_cases.input: reviews missing for an appid whose appdetails succeeded
edge_cases.expected_behavior: review_count falls back to the SteamSpy-derived positive+negative sum, review_count_source='steamspy_fallback'

edge_cases.input: review_positive_pct sourced from Steam reviews reports as an integer percentage like 87 in some payload variants
edge_cases.expected_behavior: normalized to 0.87 (divided by 100 when detected as > 1)
genres_json/categories_json become '[]', not null, so downstream json.loads never fails

edge_cases.input: size_bytes reported as a string in the payload (observed SteamSpy/Steam API inconsistency)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: coerced to int; a non-numeric string becomes NaN and is recorded in missing_fields_json

unit_tests.name: test_normalize_features_success_path
unit_tests.description: A fixture bundle with fully successful appdetails/reviews produces a fully populated row with correct dtypes.

unit_tests.name: test_normalize_features_appdetails_failure
unit_tests.description: success=false yields is_game=False and NaN derived columns, row still present.

unit_tests.name: test_review_count_fallback_to_steamspy
unit_tests.description: A missing reviews entry falls back to SteamSpy positive+negative with review_count_source='steamspy_fallback'.

unit_tests.name: test_review_positive_pct_normalized_to_ratio
unit_tests.description: An integer-percentage input of 87 is normalized to 0.87.
